claim: On any time interval \(I\) for which the zero-extended aquifer profile is identically dry on a fixed open spatial interval \(U\), a distributional solution of the printed full-line Boussinesq equation \(h_t=k\partial_x(h\partial_x h)+v_s\partial_x h-\phi h+N(t)/n\) must satisfy \(N(t)=0\) almost everywhere on \(I\). Therefore a compactly supported zero extension is incompatible with a spatially uniform additive source/sink whenever \(N\) is nonzero on a positive-measure subset of \(I\), unless the equation is restricted to the wet region or the source is explicitly localized there.

correctness.rationale: The proof is a direct distributional restriction of the printed PDE to \(U	imes I\). On that cylinder \(h\), \(h_t\), \(h_x\), and \(\partial_x(h\,h_x)\) vanish; with \(n>0\), the remaining equation forces \(N=0\) almost everywhere. The statement explicitly limits itself to a full-line PDE interpretation.

originality.rationale: The accepted contribution is the source-specific compatibility diagnosis, not the elementary general observation in isolation. No directly equivalent published analysis of the Bartlett–Porporato zero extension with additive \(N(t)\) was found in the inspected literature. The conclusion is carefully conditional on the full-line PDE interpretation.
residual_risks: The original authors may have intended the PDE to hold only on the saturated region; under that interpretation the issue is a missing domain/source qualification, not failure of the interior formula.
The proof establishes a necessary compatibility condition only. It does not prove that localizing N(t) to the wet set is sufficient for existence or for all free-boundary conditions.

value.rationale: The condition marks a concrete validity boundary for a published groundwater profile intended to represent recharge and other source/sink fluxes. It tells model users exactly when a finite zero-extended wetting-front solution cannot represent the printed equation, and what modeling qualification is needed for \(N(t)\). This is a narrow model-specific correction, not a claim of a new general porous-medium theorem.
